cards.title: Lien 1 — roadside context, unresolved access
cards.teachingJob: Show why an apparent roadside parcel still needs registry, frontage, possession, planning, and condition research.
cards.mapSubtitle: A visible road relationship is a clue, not access proof.
publicMapObservations: One published PID resolved to one NSPRD polygon feature.
NS Aerial and the parcel graphic provide dated roadside context.
unresolvedQuestions: Does registry evidence establish frontage or another legal access right?
What are the current title, possession, and physical-condition facts?
What does current planning permit, and what servicing evidence exists?
limitations: Mapped road proximity is not legal access.
The graphical parcel is not a survey; the card is not a title opinion.
Imagery does not establish occupancy, current condition, value, or permission to enter.

cards.title: Lien 8 — a mine record is a question, not a verdict
cards.teachingJob: Put the published Soapstone Mine location beside the official abandoned-mine inventory while preserving completeness, position, subsidence, and professional-review limits.
cards.mapSubtitle: Four official Soapstone Mine records are mapped; two are nearly co-located.
publicMapObservations: One published PID resolved to one NSPRD polygon feature.
The official 2024 AMO dataset contains four Brigend Brook (Soapstone Mine) opening records; the render reports their measured map distance from the parcel.
unresolvedQuestions: Do recorded or undocumented mine workings affect the parcel or intended use?
What field, geotechnical, environmental, or agency review is appropriate?
What do title, mineral-rights, access, planning, and current site evidence establish?
limitations: The AMO inventory is incomplete and excludes subsidence expressions.
The Province says private-land AMO positions could be off by up to about 50 metres.
A mapped record is not a parcel-specific hazard finding; mapped road proximity is not legal access, and this card is not a title opinion.

cards.title: Lien 11 — one lien, three parcel identifiers
cards.teachingJob: Keep a multi-PID municipal entry together and show why polygon count must not be mistaken for the number of sale entries.
cards.mapSubtitle: Three PIDs belong to one published lien entry.
publicMapObservations: Three published PIDs resolved to three NSPRD polygon features.
The three graphical features appear contiguous at this map scale.
unresolvedQuestions: What legal interest is offered across the three PIDs?
Does each PID have lawful access, and do any rights or burdens differ?
How do planning, services, possession, condition, and intended use apply to the group?
limitations: Apparent graphical contiguity does not merge titles or prove a common boundary.
Mapped road proximity is not legal access.
The graphical parcels are not surveys; this card is not a title opinion or recommendation.
